Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Discussion, Conclusion). Ideas are articulated logically, with explicit contributions listed. Task clustering via gap statistic and entropy analysis are explained with equations and tables. Minor issues include internal file paths in figure captions and some repetition in limitations.

Novelty.justification: Presents the first systematic gap statistic clustering (k*=3) of 21 LongBench tasks under 6 compression configs and validates attention entropy as a domain discriminator (η²=0.522). Builds directly on H2O/StreamingLLM but introduces task-conditioned routing hypothesis. Not groundbreaking but provides measurable empirical structure absent in prior uniform-compression literature.

Soundness.justification: Core H-M2 experiment fails (p=0.326) with baseline accuracy of only 6.7%, rendering retention ratios unreliable. Code implements simulated truncation rather than true H2O attention-based eviction; silhouette score 0.411 falls below 0.5 target. Response matrix and entropy results appear generated but downstream causal claims are unsupported. Multiple evaluation limitations explicitly acknowledged.

Significance.justification: Addresses timely problem of memory-efficient long-context inference and challenges one-size-fits-all KV cache assumption. Large effect size for entropy discrimination is notable, yet inconclusive tolerance experiment, single-model scope (Llama-2-7B), and absence of implemented router limit practical impact. Establishes foundation but does not deliver deployable system.

strengths: Rigorous gap-statistic clustering with B=500 bootstraps and interpretable task groups
Large, statistically significant entropy-domain effect (F=38.05, p<10^{-25}, η²=0.522)
weaknesses: Key H-M2 hypothesis test fails due to 6.7% baseline accuracy and inadequate metrics
Eviction implemented via input truncation rather than attention-based H2O; results unreliable
